newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse dips, volume low as T-bills attract.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse dips, volume low as T-bills attract.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index lost five points to 3022.87 on Thursday, reflecting reduced prices in key shares in a calm market.
Volume was down to 185,471 shares traded for 6.289 million shillings from 357,825 shares traded for 19.971 million shillings on Wednesday, floor dealers and bourse officials said.
"The market experienced reduced activity with many small lots changing hands," a broker said.
Market interest was in sisal concern Rea Vipingo Plantations Ltd and Kenya Airways and brokers said in the absence of market-moving news, relatively new issues attracted investor attention.
Rea Vipingo Plantations traded 15,140 share at a reduced price of 10.45 shillings while Kenya Airways traded 57,226 shares at 9.60 shillings from 9.55 on Wednesday.
National Bank of Kenya traded 28,075 shares at 15.30, unchanged from Wednesday.
Kenya Breweries traded 6,986 shares at 45.50. Foreign investors also bought 4,300 shares at 45.75 in the firm.
"Kenya Breweries appears to be attracting interest because they are trading after a dividend of 3.50 shillings," said a broker.

Brokers attributed the low market activity to a general shift of funds from the bourse to the treasury bills market which appeared attractive because of higher interest rates -- currently in the range of 18-25 percent.
"In the long term, the market is likely to remain depressed unless interest rates on treasury bills drop," a broker said.
